Vincee ColeAug 1 6 mins readHuawei's Mate 90 Pro Max Leak Shows a Phone Built to Outsmart Sanctions Vincee ColeAug 8 5 mins readHonor Robot Phone vs Pixel 11: Two Flagships, One Launch Day Marko NguyenAug 7 4 mins readGemini Robotics 2 gives Google’s robots full-body intelligence Temaz TraAug 3 4 mins readSponsored Share this post X LinkedIn Email Facebook Copy linkTL;DRNo single number measures the open-weight ecosystem. Repository downloads, routed tokens, curated model counts, benchmark entries and forecast revenue answer different questions and cannot be added together.Activity is large and heavily concentrated. The 30 July 2026 Hugging Face top-1,000 all-model sample recorded about 2.54 billion monthly downloads. Inside the text-generation top-1,000 sample, the top 100 repositories took 68.83 percent of sample activity.Qwen is the dominant family by every activity measure used here, at 36.32 percent of text-generation sample downloads and 942.1 million cumulative ATOM downloads against Llama’s 476.0 million.The capability gap is narrow. Stanford’s March 2026 snapshot put the leading closed model 49 Arena points ahead of the leading open-weight model. Kimi K3 led open weights on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at a rounded 57.Open-weight API access is cheaper by roughly eight times on list prices, averaging 0.23 dollars per million tokens against 1.86 for closed models in a May to September 2025 study, with a median capability catch-up interval of 13 weeks.License labels are a screening signal, not legal clearance. Almost 70 percent of scanned Hugging Face repositories carried no license tag at all in May 2026.Memory, not capability, is the first hard limit. Weight-only INT4 floors among audited models run from 10.8 GB for gpt-oss-20b to 1,390 GB for Kimi K3, which is 96.5 percent of an entire eight-GPU DGX B200 before any cache or runtime overhead.Open-weight models now span thousands of releases, billions of monthly repository requests and a rapidly changing mix of licenses, architectures and deployment costs. This report brings the main 2026 indicators into one source-backed view, with clear denominators and practical limits for every statistic.How to read these numbersOpen-weight AI model statistics are easy to quote and surprisingly easy to misread. A download is not a deployment, a repository is not always a distinct model, and a benchmark score says nothing about license rights or the GPU memory a model needs in production.Rather than repeating that warning after every statistic, this report states the rules once. They apply everywhere below.Table 1. Interpretation rules applied throughout this report. Figures from earlier studies retain their original period rather than being restated to the cutoff.The central finding is that open-weight AI has become a major deployment layer. Scale and activity rose quickly, leading model families shifted, and the capability gap narrowed. What has not kept pace is documentation, evaluation practice and license clarity.
